hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built (API, database role, exports, reports, jobs, files)
G1 gate catches tenant leaks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
Plants are in plants/r13-plants.diff. The run was the planted .NET gate and identity suites through verify-slot (plants/plant-run.sh, plant-inside.sh, run-server/gates.log). Both plants were live on a planted stack (plants/plant-demo.txt).

- L1: GET /api/identity/users/{id} answers from a DI-singleton memo keyed by id only. Tenant A read B's user (200). It was caught by G1HttpIsolation (86 leaks), G1NonInterference and G1ProcessState ('singleton ...UserAnswerMemo.Items').
- L2: this round's DeviceApproval migration replaces identity.sign_in_attempts' tenant_isolation policy with USING (true). Bound to A, erp_app saw other tenants' rows. It was caught by both G1DatabaseIsolation tests ('tenant A sees 3 rows of other tenants'; the policy is not the standard one).

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions of the product as built (restricted roles, escalation, screens hide)
G2 gate catches actions with no permission check planted in this piece's API (devices/approve)
hard_gates.evidence:
Both plants were live on the planted stack (plants/plant-demo.txt), and both were caught (run-server/gates.log).

- P1: POST /api/identity/users/{id}/devices/approve requires identity.profile.update instead of identity.users.update. An auditor without users.update let a device in (200). Caught by G2PermissionTests: 'declares identity.profile.update; the reviewed map identity.txt says identity.users.update'.
- P2: the same endpoint skips TargetProblemAsync. The auditor let a device of the Administrator in (200). Caught by G1CompanyIsolation ('company X administrator -> POST .../devices/approve ... answered 200, expected a refusal'), the G2AccountTakeover tests and G1SignInThrottle (approving oneself answered OK, expected Forbidden).

hard_gates.gate: G2 gate catches a screen offering an action the user cannot do, planted in this piece's own new screen (screens hide what the user cannot do)
hard_gates.evidence:
Plant U1 was MISSED.

The plant is one line in web/src/modules/identity/UserPanel.tsx HistoryTab (plants/r13-plants.diff): `const canApprove = canUnblock && (sharedPaused || !!history?.deviceApprovalUntil)` loses `canUnblock &&`.

It is live. A user whose role grants only identity.users.read and identity.signIns.read opens a paused user's Sign-in history. The planted screen offers them 'Let a device sign in': the device code field, the 'Let it in' button and the palette command identity.users.approveDevice (screenshot 10). The shipped product offers none of it (screenshot 11, walks/u1-check-*.txt).

Nothing caught it:
- The web unit suite passed 528/528 with the plant (plants/web-U1-planted-full.log). That suite includes the identity screens' permission gate and the palette and keyboard sweeps, and the identity plant self-test still reports '13 plants, all caught'; none of those plants is this one.
- The e2e suite against the planted stack passed 111 and failed 2 (plants/e2e-planted.log). Both failures came from L1's stale memo: an edited e-mail and a language read back old. Neither is about the device form.
- The only device-form tests are positive (screens.test.tsx 'lets one device in...', sign-in.spec.ts:132).

biggest_gap.title: The screen permission gate does not cover this round's new 'Let a device sign in' form: a planted fault that offers it to anyone who can read the sign-in history passes every web unit, sweep and e2e test
biggest_gap.detail:
This round added device approval to the user's Sign-in history tab. The form has a device code field, a 'Let it in' button and the palette command identity.users.approveDevice. In the shipped product it shows only when canUnblock holds (identity.users.update, and the user is within the caller's access).

It works: screenshots 03 to 06, walks w2 in English and Arabic. Another tenant's admin gets 404, a helpdesk role is refused the Administrator, and a second fresh browser stays paused.

But nothing checks the negative case, so the bar's 'screens hide what the user cannot do' is unguarded on this piece's newest screen. Remove `canUnblock &&` from canApprove and the form and its palette command are offered to a user who may only read the history (identity.signIns.read). Examples are an auditor or a branch supervisor, or an administrator looking at someone who also works in a company they do not. All 528 web unit tests pass anyway, including the identity screens' permission gate and the palette and keyboard sweeps. The identity plant self-test still reports 13 of 13 caught, and e2e shows nothing.

The server refuses the submit, so this is not a hole today. But the next edit to HistoryTab can ship it unseen.

Fix:
- Add the device form and its command to the identity screens' permission gate. Render the History tab of a paused user (shared gateway, and a pending approval) for a user with users.read and signIns.read only, and for one whose target is refused. Assert no device code field, no 'Let it in' and no enabled identity.users.approveDevice in the palette.
- Add this exact plant to scripts/identity-plant-self-test.mjs so the gate must catch it.
- Also hide or reword the advice 'enter the device code their sign-in screen shows below' for viewers who have no form below (screenshot 11).
biggest_gap.evidence:
1. In a scratch clone, apply plants/r13-plants.diff, or just the UserPanel.tsx hunk: `const canApprove = (sharedPaused || !!history?.deviceApprovalUntil);`.
2. Run `cd web && npx vitest run`: 40 files and 528 tests pass. Then `node scripts/identity-plant-self-test.mjs`: '13 plants, all caught'. Logs: plants/web-U1-planted-full.log.
3. Live check, on the planted and then the shipped stack:
- walks/mk-auditor.mjs creates a role with identity.users.read, identity.signIns.read and identity.profile.update, and a user holding it;
- walks/u1-check.mjs makes 5 anonymous failures on accountant@alnoor.example, signs in as the auditor and opens the Sign-in history.
- Planted: 'device code field offered: 1; Let it in buttons: 1' (screenshot 10). Shipped: 0 and 0 (screenshot 11).
4. The e2e suite on the planted stack: 111 passed and 2 failed, both from plant L1's stale memo; none touches the device form (plants/e2e-planted.log).

other_findings:
Round 12's biggest gap is only partly fixed, and the sign-in rate limit is still a denial of service for everyone behind the shipped gateway.

The pause side works now. A paused fresh browser on the shared address gets a device code in English and Arabic, and the user or an administrator lets exactly that browser in (attacks/device-approval.txt, walks w2).

The rate limit was only raised. It is now partitioned per account typed, under a shared-address ceiling of SignInPerMinute x SharedAddressClients = 600 a minute. One anonymous script sent 620 sign-ins at 620 made-up e-mail addresses in 12.4 s ({401: 580, 429: 40}; the earlier 20 came from my own probes). Right after it, admin@gulfsteel.example, admin@alnoor.example and admin.ar@alnoor.example with their right passwords from other browsers all answered 429 request.tooMany (attacks/shared-ceiling.txt). About 10 requests a second keeps every user of every workspace out.

The root cause is unchanged: the one-command deployment still does not see client addresses (no reverse proxy, ERP_KNOWN_PROXIES empty). SignInRateLimit.cs is p03's; the GlobalLimiter in ErpPlatform is p00's kernel.

The audit trail keeps the device approval's hash in clear (audit.entries changes.device_approval_hash old and new). It is an unkeyed SHA-256 of an 8-symbol code (31^8, about 8.5e11), so it can be reversed offline. Password and token hashes are redacted.

The impact is low, because a code only works with that browser's signed erp_pending cookie. It should still be redacted like the other credentials.

The administrators' approve endpoint accepts any well-formed code (200 'until ...'), because the server cannot check it, and a new approval replaces the last. An administrator's typo silently overwrites a correct approval made a minute earlier. Showing the last few characters, or asking the person to read the code back, would help.

Keyboard: after G then U, the focus is already in the users search box. The footer hint '/ search' then types a literal '/'. A user who follows the hint and types an e-mail gets 'Nothing matches' (q=%2Faccountant...; walks/probe3.mjs: after '/', INPUT value '/').
Still open since round 9: with a record open at 1366 px, the users list truncates the 'Language' header ('Langu…'; screenshots 02 and 10).

Keyboard-first margins are still thin:
- The all-keyboard create-restricted-user path wins by one keystroke (45 against 46).
- In find-user, only 'initials' (3 keys) wins; 'shortest' (8), 'prefixes' (15), 'row' (20), 'enter' (21) and 'palette' (29) lose on keystrokes to Odoo's 5.

Verify processor time has little headroom.
- Run 1, under load (highest 83.59, with another critic's verify and my demo, comparisons and planted e2e stack beside it): 10,891 s, over the 10,500 maximum. Every test was green.
- Run 2, quieter (highest 45.2): 9,559 s, passed.
- The integrator's alone run: 9,135 s.
The owner has needs-human #22 open on this.

Fixed since round 12 and still fixed:
- A valid set-up code still signs in from a paused shared address.
- A known device (device cookie) is not paused by others' failures.
- The sign-in history labels 172.x as 'shared gateway' / 'بوابة مشتركة'.
- 'Roles in one company' starts at 'Choose a role'.
- Matrix search 'عرض' plus 'Select all shown' ticks exactly 9 view permissions in Arabic (walks/w3-roles-ar.txt).
- Copy and Delete role are in the palette.
- 'What they can do' names each granting role and its company in Arabic (screenshot 08).

Positive:
- The pause answer has the same keys (deviceCode, sharedAddress, pausedUntil) for an account that exists and for one that does not.
- An approval is used up by the first sign-in, after which the browser is a known device.
- Another fresh browser behind the address stays paused.
- No console errors or 5xx in any walk, in English or Arabic.
